summary: All ten findings confirmed. Finding 1 is stronger than stated: the unproved step in the proof of Proposition 5.4 is false inside the paper's own hypotheses (a trivial-trace example), and Proposition 5.4 survives only through Néron models. Findings 2, 3, 6, 8 and 10 are confirmed with corrected or completed fixes: finding 3's gap can be closed in full (Proposition 3.2 holds without algebraic independence, by an induction the paper's Lemmas 3.3–3.4 support), finding 6's [m]-degree fact is already planned at A3, finding 8 needs only an expanded note, and finding 10's reference is completed. Worked from arXiv:2108.09722v1; the published Inventiones text was not accessible.

findings.reason:
Checked against arXiv:2108.09722v1 (the only arXiv version; the Inventiones text was not available, so everything below is about v1). Quote: on p. 25 (page image), in the proof of Proposition 5.4, the text reads 'Denote by 𝒜′ (resp. ℬ) the Zariski closure of A′ in 𝒜 (resp. B in 𝒜 ×_S 𝒜). Both 𝒜′ and ℬ are abelian schemes over S.' No argument is given. Use: p. 26 then applies Proposition 2.1 with g = h : ℬ → 𝒜′, which needs a flat morphism between smooth projective varieties. It applies Proposition 4.2 to 𝒜′, which needs an abelian scheme, and Lemma 4.1(4) and §4.3 to ℬ. Setting: from (a)–(d) on p. 22 (image checked), S is a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field k. A has good reduction over all of S and trivial K̄/k-trace (the printed hypothesis is the K̄-trace). By (e), A′ = X_r is an abelian subvariety of A. The extraction item PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/good-reduction-model states the second clause with no trace hypothesis: 'abelian subvarieties of A have Zariski closures that are abelian subschemes'. None of E1–E15 and nothing in REV-PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22 touches this step. The claim of the finding is accurate.

The counterexample, checked step by step. (i) E is supersingular, so E[F] = α_p and (E×E)[F] = α_p². The order-p subgroups of α_p² are the images of t ↦ (at, bt), one for each (a:b) in P¹(k). On the chart b = 1 the family is the closed subscheme x = ay of α_p² × A¹, that is k[a][x,y]/(x^p, y^p, x − ay) = k[a][y]/(y^p). This is free of rank p over k[a]. It is a subgroup because the equation is linear, and the two charts agree where a is a unit. Equivalently, G is the height-one subgroup attached to the tautological line O(−1) ⊂ O² = Lie(E²)⊗O_{P¹}. Every line is p-stable here because the p-map on Lie(E) is zero for supersingular E. So G is a finite flat subgroup scheme of order p over P¹. (ii) The quotient of an abelian scheme by a finite locally free subgroup scheme is an abelian scheme; this one is Moret-Bailly's family over P¹. The second factor C₀/G_{λ₀} × P¹ is constant. Hence the product A is an abelian scheme over the projective base P¹, and A_K has good reduction everywhere. (iii) ker i = G ∩ (G_{λ₀} × P¹). On the fibre at λ = (a:1) the equations x = ay and x = a₀y give (a − a₀)y = 0. So the kernel is trivial for λ ≠ λ₀, including the generic point, where a − a₀ ≠ 0 in K. It is G_{λ₀} ≅ α_p at λ₀. So i_K is a proper monomorphism, hence a closed immersion, and B = i_K(C₀,K) is an abelian subvariety. (iv) C₀ × P¹ is integral and i is proper, so the reduced image of i is the scheme-theoretic closure 𝒳 of B. The morphism i : C₀ × P¹ → 𝒳 is proper, quasi-finite and birational, hence finite birational. The multiplicity of the fibre 𝒳_{λ₀} along D = i_{λ₀}(C₀) is p. Fulton's Prop. 10.1(a) (specialisation commutes with proper push-forward) gives this. So does a direct degree count: for L ample on A, the fibre degrees (i*L)² on C₀ × P¹ and deg_L 𝒳_λ are constant in λ, and at λ₀ the projection formula gives (i*L)² = p·deg_L D. So 𝒳_{λ₀} is non-reduced and 𝒳 is not an abelian scheme. Also, 𝒳 is not normal: if it were, the finite birational map i would be an isomorphism by Zariski's Main Theorem. So 𝒳 is not smooth over k. The closure of the corresponding B ⊂ A×A is 𝒜 ×_S 𝒳, which is not smooth either. Hence Proposition 2.1 and Proposition 4.2 do not apply to the printed 𝒜′ and ℬ. The mechanism needs a non-étale kernel, and in characteristic 0 the clause is true. So the example refutes the item exactly as stated. It has non-trivial trace, but the item carries no trace hypothesis, so it is a valid counterexample to the item.

Stronger than the finding says: the printed step is false even inside the paper's setting (a)–(e), not merely unproved. Here is a sketch I checked. Take a smooth projective curve S and a non-isotrivial, generically ordinary abelian surface 𝒞 → S. One exists: normalise a general complete-intersection curve in the minimal compactification of A_{2,n} ⊗ k (n ≥ 3, p ∤ n). The boundary has dimension 1, so the curve misses it. The Hasse invariant is a section of ω^{p−1}, and ω has positive degree on S. So 𝒞 has a non-ordinary fibre, and for a general curve that fibre has p-rank 1. 𝒞_K has trivial K̄/k-trace. A constant isogeny factor of dimension 2 would make every fibre isogenous to one fixed ordinary surface. A factor of dimension 1 would leave an elliptic curve with good reduction everywhere over a projective curve; such a curve is isotrivial, and the same contradiction follows. After a finite separable base change, the p+1 subgroups μ_p ⊂ 𝒞_K[F] are rational. Their flat closures in 𝒞[F] are finite flat subgroups of order p. At a p-rank-1 fibre, 𝒞_s[F] = μ_p × α_p has exactly two subgroups of order p, so two of the closures, G ≠ H, coincide there. Then A := (𝒞/G ×_S 𝒞/H)_K has good reduction everywhere and trivial K̄/k-trace, being isogenous to 𝒞_K². A′ := image of 𝒞_K is an abelian subvariety, and the argument of (iii)–(iv) shows that its closure has a fibre of multiplicity p. With X = A′ (r = 1, X_0 = 0), which has a dense set of small points, (a)–(e) hold and the printed sentence is false. So under PROTOCOL §18 this is an error, 'a step that fails', rather than a gap.

The fix works. A′ has good reduction: by Poincaré reducibility A is isogenous to A′ × A/A′, and good reduction is preserved under isogeny and passes to the factors of a product. So the Néron model 𝒜′_N of A′ is an abelian scheme over S. Using B ≅ A × A′, (x, z) ↦ (x, z − x), the Néron model of B is ℬ_N = 𝒜 ×_S 𝒜′_N. In these coordinates the sum map is the second projection, which is smooth, hence flat. 𝒜′_N and ℬ_N are smooth projective varieties over k, and 𝒴 := closure of Y in ℬ_N surjects onto 𝒜′_N. For 𝒯 a torsion multi-section of 𝒜′_N of order prime to p (E2), 𝒯 is finite étale over S, hence smooth. So Proposition 2.1, Proposition 4.2 and Lemma 4.1(4) apply verbatim, with h*ℒ_{𝒜′} symmetric and rigidified because h is a homomorphism. §4.3 computes ĥ(Y) and ĥ(Z_i) on ℬ_N. Height zero in B is equivalent to height zero in A × A, since a symmetric ample bundle on A×A restricts to one on B, and the paper already uses this equivalence. So Proposition 5.4 and Theorem 1.1 survive, and the error affects the proof only.

Adjustments to the fix. (1) The replacement clause for good-reduction-model is right. Add that the extended homomorphism is a closed immersion, so the closure is an abelian subscheme, in characteristic 0 or whenever its kernel is étale. Add NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.5 to planned beside R11.1: R11.1 has the Néron model, the mapping property and 'Compare good reduction with an abelian-scheme model', but 'A′ has good reduction' is the preservation of good reduction under isogeny that R11.5 plans ('Establish preservation of good reduction under isogeny'). (2) Record E16 with kind 'error', not 'gap', and affects 'the proof'. The reason should give the trivial-trace example above, since the Moret-Bailly example, whose trace is non-trivial, only shows the mechanism and does not satisfy (d). known 'new'. Add E16's locator to the 'published-version' collation gap, whose item list already contains prop-5-4. (3) The prop-5-4 note and the Part II brief should say that 𝒜′ and ℬ are the Néron models of A′ and B, and should cite E16 next to E2.

Confirmed. Scope: arXiv:2108.09722v1, the only accessible text, read on the page images of pp. 15-16 and 18-19. The Inventiones text was not available, so this verdict is about v1 only. (1) Definitions. §3.2 (p. 15): for K/k with k algebraically closed in K, I(K/k) is 'the set of intermediate fields k' of K/k which is algebraically closed in K'. It covers every transcendence degree, including k and K themselves. So I(K̄/k̄) is the set of algebraically closed fields between k̄ and K̄. Specialness for A/K/k' is defined by (3.3), which uses only A_K̄ and the algebraic closure of k' in K̄. (2) The map is well defined but not injective. If f in K is algebraic over k' ∩ K, then f is algebraic over k', so f lies in k'. Hence φ(k') = k' ∩ K is algebraically closed in K and contains k. φ preserves order, and it is surjective, because sending k'' to its algebraic closure in K̄ is a section. So the claimed bijection fails exactly at injectivity, as the finding says. (3) The counterexample, step by step. Take k algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ 2 and K = k(s,t), in which k is algebraically closed. Set u = √s + t and k' = k(u)‾ in K̄, so k' ∈ I(K̄/k̄) and k' ≠ k̄. Since K(√s)/K is separable of degree 2, there is σ in Aut(K̄/K) with σ(√s) = −√s; put u' = σu = −√s + t. If f in K is algebraic over k(u), then f = σf is algebraic over k(u'). Now k(u,u') = k(√s,t) has transcendence degree 2. A g that is transcendental over k and algebraic over both k(u) and k(u') would make u and u' both algebraic over k(g), which is impossible. So f ∈ k, and φ(k') = k = φ(k̄). Now the equivalence. Let E/k be an elliptic curve, A = E_K, and P ∈ E(k') with x(P) = u; P exists because k' is algebraically closed. The K̄/k'-trace of E_K̄ is E_{k'} with tr the identity, so X = {P} is special for A_K̄/K̄/k' (take Y = {P}, T = 0). Specialness for A/K/φ(k') = A/K/k would give P = Q + τ with Q ∈ E(k) and τ torsion. Every torsion point of E_K̄ lies in E(k), so P ∈ E(k) and u = x(P) ∈ k, which is false. So both claims in the first paragraph of the proof fail, and 'we may assume that k and K are algebraically closed' does not follow. One correction to the evidence: as written the example needs char k ≠ 2. In characteristic 2, √s is purely inseparable over K, no σ moves it, and u² = s + t² ∈ K, so φ(k') ≠ k. Because the paper claims every characteristic, one characteristic is enough to refute it. A version valid in every characteristic uses u = s^{1/ℓ} + t with ℓ a prime different from char k, and σ multiplying s^{1/ℓ} by a primitive ℓ-th root of unity ζ. Then u − σu = (1−ζ)s^{1/ℓ}, so again k(u,σu) = k(s^{1/ℓ},t). (4) The statement is still true. The statement of Proposition 3.6, as item prop-3-6 copies it, follows from the algebraically closed case by the fix's Galois argument, which I checked. Let F ∈ I(K̄/k̄) be the field for K̄/k̄. Let F'' be the algebraic closure in K̄ of the compositum of all σ(F), σ ∈ Aut(K̄/K). Then F'' is Aut(K̄/K)-stable. Every x in F'' has all its K-conjugates in F'', so the minimal polynomial of x over K has coefficients in F'' ∩ K. Hence F'' is algebraic over k_{A,X} := F'' ∩ K, and k_{A,X} ∈ I(K/k). Let k' ∈ I(K/k), and write (k')‾ for its algebraic closure in K̄, which is Aut(K̄/K)-stable. X is special for A/K/k' iff F ⊆ (k')‾, iff F'' ⊆ (k')‾, iff k_{A,X} ⊆ k'. For the last step: ⇒ holds because F'' ∩ K ⊆ (k')‾ ∩ K = k'; ⇐ holds because F'' is algebraic over k_{A,X}. Three corrections to the fix text. (i) 'Finitely many conjugates' needs trdeg(F/k̄) < ∞. The construction gives this, but the statement of Proposition 3.6 does not, so use the compositum of all conjugates and drop 'finitely many'. (ii) The justification through K^perf is right but roundabout; the minimal-polynomial argument above is enough. (iii) The algebraically closed case itself rests on Corollary 3.5(i), through the printed proof and through E1's repair. The proof of Corollary 3.5(i) has the gap of finding 3, so E17 should cross-reference E18. (5) Theorem 1.1 survives, as the finding says. In Proposition 3.1, 'X special for A/K/k_i' means special for A_K̄/K̄/k̄_i. The algebraically closed case gives a field F with F ⊆ k̄_1 ∩ k̄_2. That intersection is k: a transcendental g in both would give k̄_1 = k(g)‾ = k̄_2, hence k_1 = k̄_1 ∩ K = k_2, contradicting k_1 ≠ k_2 (E5). So F = k, and X is special for A/K/k. (6) The finding is not redundant. E1 is about the first case after the reduction. Its reason, the note on prop-3-6 and the review ('No further mistake was found') say nothing about φ, and none of E1-E15 records it. Medium is the right severity: the proof route the design brief would follow is wrong, but the statement and Theorem 1.1 stand.

Confirmed, with a better fix: the dependent case can be proved, see (5). Scope: arXiv v1, read on the page images of pp. 13-15. (1) The geometric argument. The proof uses a flat, quasi-finite ψ : U → S₁ × S₂, where k(U) is finite over the compositum k(S₁)k(S₂) and the algebraic closure of k(S_i) is k_i. So dim U = trdeg(k₁k₂/k). A flat quasi-finite morphism is open with finite fibres, so it forces dim U = dim S₁ + dim S₂. That means trdeg(k₁k₂/k) = trdeg(k₁/k) + trdeg(k₂/k), which is algebraic independence. Without independence, ψ(U) lies in a proper closed Z ⊂ S₁ × S₂ that dominates both factors. For general s₂, the fibre of Z over s₂ has dimension trdeg(k₁k₂) − trdeg(k₂) < dim S₁. So V does not dominate S₁, and 'Because k(V)/k(S₁) is finite' (p. 14) fails. In the independent case the printed proof is fine: flatness makes every component V dominate S₁ × s₂. (2) The statement assumes only k₁ ∩ k₂ = k, and this does not give independence. I checked the finding's example k₁ = k(x,y)‾ and k₂ = k(z, x+yz)‾ inside k(x,y,z)‾. Their compositum has transcendence degree 3 < 4. They meet in k by the finding's derivation argument, which is correct in every characteristic. Take g in both, and a p-power g' of g separable over k(x,y) and over k(z, x+yz). Then ∂_z g' = 0 and (z∂_x − ∂_y)g' = 0. Since z is transcendental over k(x,y,g'), both partials vanish, so dg' = 0. The same holds for g'^{1/p}, which again lies in both fields and is separable over both. So g' lies in the intersection of all M^{p^n}, where M is the separable closure of k(x,y,z), and is therefore algebraic over k. Geometrically: the fibres of (x,y,z) ↦ (z, x+yz) project to the lines x + z₀y = w₀ in the (x,y)-plane, and any two points of that plane are joined by at most two such lines. (3) Corollary 3.5(i) applies Proposition 3.2 with base k' ∩ k_A to k' ∈ I and k_A, and nothing in its proof controls how these two fields sit relative to each other. If the corollary holds, then every k' ∈ I contains k_A, so the pair is independent over k_A after the fact. A dependent pair in I would therefore itself be a counterexample, and the gap is exactly the dependent case of Proposition 3.2. Everything built on k_A inherits the gap: Corollary 3.5(i), Proposition 3.6 (the printed first case and E1's repair) and hence the paper's route to Proposition 3.1. (4) The finding is not redundant. Among E1-E15 only E8 touches Corollary 3.5, and E8 is the misprint '⊆ I'. The review found 'no further mistake'. (5) Repair (b) checks, and so does a proof of (a). Repair (b) is correct, with one precision. The reductions to Stab⁰(X) = 0 and T_X = A replace A by abelian varieties over K̄. So the argument must run in K̄ with the fields F_i = k̄_i, not k_i. The F_i meet in k and are independent, because distinct algebraically closed fields of transcendence degree 1 are, and K̄ has finite transcendence degree. Suppose X is special for A/K̄/F_i. Then X = tr(Y⊗K̄) + a + C with C ⊆ Stab⁰(X) = 0, so X ⊆ tr(Tr⊗K̄) + a, and T_X = A makes the trace map surjective. In characteristic p the trace map is a purely inseparable isogeny onto its image, so A is defined over F_i up to isogeny. Proposition 3.2 in the independent case gives Φ : A → A₀ ⊗ K̄ with A₀ over k. Over F ⊇ k, Φ(X) is special iff Φ(X) is defined over F, because torsion points of A₀ ⊗ K̄ lie in A₀(k). Lemma 3.4, which needs no independence, then gives Φ(X) defined over k, so X is special for A/K/k. Option (a), which the red team left open, can be supplied. Proposition 3.2 holds in every characteristic without independence, by induction on the defect δ = trdeg k₁ + trdeg k₂ − trdeg(k₁k₂), using only the independent case and the paper's Lemmas 3.3 and 3.4. Write k₁ = k(c)‾ and k₂ = k(b)‾ with b, c finite tuples, K = (k₁k₂)‾ and δ > 0. Choose a k₁-embedding τ of K into an algebraically closed field Ω of finite transcendence degree, with τK algebraically independent of K over k₁. Then K ∩ τK = k₁, so k₂ ∩ τk₂ ⊆ k₁ ∩ k₂ = k. Transporting the isogeny by τ, which fixes A₁, gives A₂ ⊗ Ω ∼ A₁ ⊗ Ω ∼ τA₂ ⊗ Ω. Count degrees with d₁ = trdeg k(c), d₂ = trdeg k(b), e = trdeg k(b,c) and a = trdeg(c / k(b,τb)). Then trdeg k(b,τb,c) = 2e − d₁, so the new defect δ' = 2d₂ − trdeg k(b,τb) equals 2δ − d₁ + a, and a ≤ trdeg(c/k₂) = d₁ − δ. Suppose a = d₁ − δ. Let L = (k₂τk₂)‾. The locus W of c over k₂ and its conjugate τW, the locus of c over τk₂, are irreducible of dimension d₁ − δ, and both contain the locus of c over L, which has the same dimension. So W_L = (τW)_L. By Lemma 3.4, W is defined over k₂ ∩ τk₂ = k, so d₁ = trdeg k(c) ≤ dim W = d₁ − δ, and δ = 0. So δ > 0 forces δ' < δ. By induction A₂ ∼ A₀ ⊗ k₂ with A₀ over k, and Lemma 3.3 over k₁ gives A₁ ∼ A₀ ⊗ k₁. I checked the defect count on the finding's example (δ = 1 → 0) and on a line through a point of A³ (δ = 2 → 1 → 0). (6) Right fix. Add E18 as the finding proposes, with kind 'gap', affects 'the proof', and the locator given. Its correction should be the induction above, which proves the dependent case, rather than the open-ended option (a). Then Proposition 3.2, Corollary 3.5(i), Proposition 3.6 and E1's repair stand as stated. The items prop-3-2 and cor-3-5-i keep their statements. Their notes, and the Part II brief (which says 'State and prove, as in Xie–Yuan … Proposition 3.2'), should say that the printed proof covers only independent k₁, k₂ and that E18 supplies the reduction. Repair (b) can be recorded as the shortest route to Proposition 3.1. Medium severity is right.

Confirmed. Worked from arXiv:2108.09722v1 (the Inventiones text was not accessible). (a) Extraction: I read all 65 items. ĥ appears only in canonical-height (existence of the limit (1.2) and independence of the model, citing Gubler), height-quadratic-bound (ĥ is a positive semi-definite quadratic form, and the bound for a sum), small-points (the comparability of two heights is asserted in passing, 'any two such heights bound each other'), good-reduction-height, northcott-trivial-trace, fundamental-inequality and height-zero-small-points. No item states (i) ĥ_{φ*L} = ĥ_L∘φ for a homomorphism or isogeny φ, (ii) ĥ_{p1*L1⊗p2*L2}(x,y) = ĥ_{L1}(x)+ĥ_{L2}(y), (iii) comparability of ĥ_L and ĥ_{L′} as its own result, (iv) behaviour under enlarging K (or k), or (v) the identification of the model height (1.1)–(1.2) with the Néron–Tate height of the M_K-structure of (S,M). (b) Paper, page images: p. 24 (Lemma 5.3) 'This induces an isogeny A → A′ with A′ = B × C … Then “small points” of X^r transfer to “small points” of X_r … its image X′ = B + t′ in A′ contains a dense set of small points of A′/K/k … Choose L = p1*L1 + p2*L2 … ĥ_L(x + t′) = ĥ_{L1}(x) + ĥ_{L2}(t′)'. Passing small points from X to X^r needs (ii). Passing them along the isogeny A → B × C needs (i) together with (iii), because φ*L is a different symmetric ample bundle on A. The decomposition of ĥ_L on B × C is (ii). p. 26 (Proposition 5.4): 'small points of X transfer to small points of Y = X_{r−1} × X. Then Y has a dense set of small points in B' uses (ii) on A × A, then (i) and (iii) for the inclusion B ⊂ A × A and the bundle ℒ_B. pp. 23–25: 'By extending K and k if necessary', 'which exists by replacing K by a finite extension', 'we may need to replacing K by a finite extension again'. These use (iv). I checked the scaling from (1.1) by the projection formula. For a point x, with S′ the normalization of S in K′ and ℒ pulled back, h_{K′}(x) = [K′(x):K]/[K′(x):K′]·h_K(x) = [K′:K]·h_K(x). So 'dense small points' and specialness do not change. (v) is needed to apply Conrad Thm 9.15 (p. 24 and §5.3), Gubler Lemma 4.1 (Lemma 5.2) and Yamaki Thm 1.5, which are stated for heights over a generalized global field or M_K-field, not for the intersection-number definition (1.1). (c) Libraries: declarations.tsv and the trees at the pins have no Néron–Tate height for general abelian varieties in either library. The only canonical heights are Tau Ceti's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight (EllipticCurve/CanonicalHeight.lean:124) and its pairing, which do not give these items. (d) Atlas: RP.0 imports 'normalized absolute heights, product formula and Northcott from the audited arithmetic-height supplier' (number fields). GZ.1 plans isogeny pullback and finite-extension independence only over number fields. DY.1 is 'over a number field', and R35 is Faltings heights. So nothing plans (i)–(v) over function fields, and 'missing' is right. The owner is right: GAO-HABEGGER-19/5–6 (heights and the Néron–Tate height over the function field of a curve) are missing and routed to RP.0 as a source, and REV accepted that route. Fix, with small changes. All uses of (i), (ii), (iv) and (v) are under (a)–(d), so trdeg 1 and K = k(S) for a curve S. State each item at least in that case, beside GH19/5–6. The general polarized (S,M) form is needed only for the comparability behind the small-points definition and for Lemma 3.7. Item (b) should cover the constant-field extension as well as finite K′/K ('extending K and k', p. 23), and cite GAO-HABEGGER-19/72, which already records that 'the canonical height of a subvariety is unchanged by extending the constant field'. All the new items get status missing and route 1 (RP.0 as a source). Also cite them in the notes of small-points and special-has-small-points. I could not open Gubler 2003/2007 here, so the theorem numbers in the fix rest on the paper's own citations.

Confirmed. Worked from arXiv:2108.09722v1. (a) Extraction: none of the 65 items states that torsion points, or torsion points of order prime to p, are Zariski dense in an abelian variety. torsion-part-etale is about 𝒜[m] → S being finite étale. manin-mumford, torsion-subvariety and special-has-small-points (cited to Lang) use density but do not state it. E2's correction says '§5.3 needs only these: prime-to-p torsion points are Zariski dense in A′, and so are those off the proper closed subset A′_{e+1}', and no item carries that. (b) Paper, page image p. 27: 'As A′(K̄)_tor ∖ A′_{e+1}(K̄) is Zariski dense in A′, X_{r−1} × X contains a Zariski dense set of torsion points of A × A.' After E2, Proposition 5.4 covers only t of order prime to char k (p. 26: 'a torsion multi-section 𝒯 … of order non-divisible by char K'), so the stronger prime-to-p density is needed. The same page also uses the density a second time. 'Therefore, f⁻¹(t) contains a Zariski dense set of torsion points of A × A' needs torsion points to be dense in each component, a torsion subvariety, of f⁻¹(t). special-has-small-points (p. 3) uses it for the torsion part T of a special X. Removing A′_{e+1} is harmless: it is a proper closed subset of the irreducible A′ (p. 25, codimension ≥ 2), and a dense set minus a proper closed subset stays dense. (c) Libraries at the pins: Tau Ceti's AbelianVariety directory (Basic, End/{Basic,BaseChange,Trivial}, Hom/{Basic,BaseChange,Iso}, Isogeny, MorphismGroup, Product, TangentSpace, Trivial) has mulBy at End/Basic.lean:243 and no torsion theory. Confirmed, with corrections to its evidence and fix. Worked from arXiv:2108.09722v1. (b) Paper, page images pp. 20–21, 26: (i) Lemma 4.1(1): '[m]*ℒ − m²ℒ is trivial over every fiber of π … so it lies in π*Pic(S)'. This is the seesaw principle. (ii) §4.3: 'ℒ − [−1]*ℒ is trivial over A, so it is isomorphic to π*ℳ'. This is true here because 𝒜 is regular and the fibres over closed points are integral, reduced divisors π*(s), so a divisor supported on fibres is π* of a divisor on S. (iii) Proposition 4.2: '([m]*ℒ)^g·([m]*ℳ) = deg([m])ℒ^g·ℳ … m^{2g+i}ℒ^g·ℳ = m^{2g}ℒ^g·ℳ'. (iv) Proposition 5.4: 'Let ℒ_{𝒜′} (resp. ℒ_ℬ) be a symmetric, relatively ample and rigidified line bundle'. Proposition 2.1 (p. 7) needs 'a flat morphism between smooth projective varieties', so 𝒜′ and ℬ must be projective over k. §4.3 also needs 𝒜 projective, because (1.1) defines heights on projective integral models. (c) Libraries: declarations.tsv and the trees at the pins have no seesaw, relative ampleness or abelian-scheme declaration. Tau Ceti has only invertible sheaves and line-bundle classes (LineBundle/*). Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry has no 'ample'. (d) Atlas: A1 plans 'the theorem of the square and cube' and A2 polarizations; neither names the seesaw principle, generic-fibre triviality or projectivity of abelian schemes. A2 explicitly refuses to assume a polarization. The evidence sentence 'No roadmap in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ contains the word seesaw' is literally false. tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_ModularCurves.json, Layer 2D, says 'establish the seesaw, biextension, descent, and arbitrary-base-change identities', and MetaplecticAutomorphicForms has theta see-saws. But the first is only for the genus-one Poincaré bundle on E ×_S E, a Tau Ceti roadmap that is not to be re-planned, and the second is unrelated. So the conclusion stands. The headline 'no cited layer plans them' is wrong for (iii). A3, which the extraction already cites, plans '[n] is finite locally free of rank n^(2g)'. The Abelian Schemes packet node A6/degree-of-an-endomorphism states 'deg [n] = n^{2g}' at field level. The degree in the projection formula is the generic degree of [m] on the integral 𝒜, which is the field-level degree on A. So (iii) is an item with status planned [A3] (A6 node as the field-level statement), not a missing one, which is what the fix's own text says. For (iv), 'used in Lemma 4.1(3)' is imprecise. Lemma 4.1(3) assumes a π-ample ℒ. What it uses is a different pair of facts, neither an item. First, for π-ample ℒ over a projective S, ℒ ⊗ π*L′ is ample for a suitable ample L′ on S (EGA II 4.6.13). Second, the pullback of an ample bundle by the finite morphism [m] is ample. Relative ampleness is in AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1 ('Include relative ampleness and very ampleness'). Name them in the lemma-4-1-3 note, as planned at R09.1 for the first and missing SF.0 for the second. Right fix. Note that A1's relative theorem of the cube for rigidified bundles would give Lemma 4.1(1) directly. (ii) Missing, routed to SF.0 with PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21/29, the same statement. Confirmed, low. Scope: arXiv v1, read on the page images of pp. 1, 5 and 16-18. (1) §1.1 (p. 1) opens with 'Let k be an algebraically closed field'. It defines a projective model of K/k as 'a normal projective variety S over k with function field K', and a polarization as a projective model with an ample M. (2) The paper uses the notion outside that scope. §1.3 (p. 5) says '(H, M|_H) is a polarization of K/k''. Lemma 3.7 (p. 17) says 'the polarization of (H, M_{k'}|_H) of K/k''. Here k' = k(P¹) is not algebraically closed. The proof (p. 17) establishes only that H is geometrically integral, and it never mentions normality. The proof of Proposition 3.1 (p. 18) uses heights for Kk̄_i/k̄_i with the model (H_i)_{k̄_i} and does not state that intersection numbers are unchanged by k_i → k̄_i. Item lemma-3-7-pencil repeats 'so (H, M_{k'}|_H) is a polarization of K/k''. (3) The finding is not redundant. E5 and E9 concern Lemma 3.7 but not this point, and no E-entry or review note mentions normality. (4) The fix is right. H geometrically integral with function field K gives that K/k_i is regular, so H_{k̄_i} is integral with function field Kk̄_i. Its normalization ν : H̃ → H_{k̄_i} is finite and birational, so (H̃, ν*M_i) is a polarization of Kk̄_i/k̄_i in the sense of §1.1, since the pullback of an ample bundle under a finite map is ample. The naive heights agree by the projection formula. The strict transform of 𝒳 maps birationally onto the closure of X over H_{k̄_i}, and the line bundles are pulled back. Intersection numbers on proper schemes are invariant under ground-field extension. So the heights agree, and the height inequality of Proposition 3.1 is for a genuine polarization. Normality plays no role in formula (1.1) itself, so the fix should also say that ĥ^{M_i} on the non-normal model is defined by the same formula. (5) A caveat on the alternative. Choosing s₀ with H₀ normal and using the openness of the geometrically normal locus for the flat proper ψ (EGA IV₃ 12.2.4) also works. But it needs a Bertini theorem for normality in every characteristic, which is not among the extraction's items; bertini-integral covers only integrality. Prefer the normalization route, or add that Bertini input as an item.

SF.5's description ('Construct Chow groups, rational equivalence, proper pushforward, flat/lci pullback, refined Gysin maps, Chern classes and intersection products … Source route. Fulton Intersection Theory') names neither the Tor formula nor associativity, and the item's note ('the length formula for proper intersections is part of that construction') covers only Fulton Prop. 7.1(b). Expand the note to say that SF.5 must supply (i) the agreement of Serre's Tor multiplicity with Fulton's for proper intersections on a smooth variety, and (ii) associativity for successive Cartier divisors, as used in the proof of Proposition 2.4. Separate missing items are not needed. Severity low is right.
